title: Sales/CS enterprise asks - compliance-aware bundling & quick econ scoping
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Problem: Sales and CS regularly surface feature requests from regulated customers (finance, healthcare) that carry non-functional compliance constraints (audit logs, KMS, region isolation). The current intake flow treats these requests the same as standard asks, leading to lengthy back-and-forth, missed signal for Dedicated/Private sales, and inaccurate early econ estimates.

Goal: Build a lightweight aggregation + rapid-scoping path in the intake pipeline that: 1) tags and bundles compliance-sensitive asks automatically, 2) produces a one-page initial scoping card (tech constraints, minimal solution, rough engineering delta, and 30/90-day economic proxy) and 3) surfaces an upsell/hand-off flag for Dedicated/Private sales. This should reduce discovery cycles by ~40% and improve initial feasibility accuracy for the GTM team.

Proposed approach: 1) Intake form addendum for compliance flags + example prompts for Sales to use when capturing asks. 2) Aggregator job (manual at first) that groups asks by account + compliance vector + impacted product area. 3) Quick-econ template (non-lined) that estimates order-of-magnitude effort and revenue path for the first release. 4) PM-run weekly triage short meeting to produce scoping cards and route to Eng/Design.

Out of scope: full engineering requirements, security design reviews, and locked pricing; those are follow-ups after initial scoping card approval.
acceptance_criteria: Intake form addendum created and linked from Sales toolkit
Aggregator process documented and run for 2 pilot accounts
Scoping card template completed and validated with one AE and one CS lead
Quick-econ worksheet returns consistent ranges for effort and potential ARR uplift for pilot cases
Routing flag added to the intake tracker to mark Dedicated/Private-worthy requests
comments: 2025-02-15 - Aisha Khan: Kickoff meeting with Sales Ops and two AEs. Sales confirm pain: they spend 2-3 syncs explaining compliance nuance. Agreed to prototype addendum and manual grouping first.

2025-02-17 - Carmen Li (Sales): Provided three recent customer asks (ACME Health, NorrBank, Helios Therapeutics) as examples. Noted that region isolation + audit retention were the dominant compliance asks.

2025-02-18 - Ben Torres: Drafted scoping card template. Key fields: account snapshot, compliance vectors, minimal viable acceptance criteria, engineering risk (L/M/H), quick effort (S/M/L), high-level econ band (<$50k, $50-200k, $200k+).
2025-02-20 - Diego Martinez (Security): Reviewed template for obvious security triggers. Suggested mandatory checkbox for KMS/HSM and an automatic escalation path if HSM required.
2025-02-22 - Aisha Khan: Ran pilot aggregator on ACME Health + NorrBank. Grouped 6 requests into 2 bundles. Generated two scoping cards and shared with Eng and AE for feedback.

2025-02-24 - Evelyn Park (Engineering PM): Feedback: scoping card effort bands are useful; recommend adding a CPU/GPU resource implication line for Dedicated discussions. Also suggested linking to existing runtime-quantization notes.

2025-02-26 - Ben Torres: Updated template and added routing flag in the intake tracker (spreadsheet prototype). Filing: Confluence doc and a Google Drive folder with pilot artifacts. Next: create a small automation to surface compliance tag from intake form answers.

2025-02-28 - Aisha Khan: Decision: ship the intake addendum + scoping card template for a 6-week pilot. Sales Ops will train five AEs. PM to run weekly triage meetings. Engineering will commit to evaluate two scoping cards per week.
